root_cause.text: The swap address space was incorrectly marked read-only (__ro_after_init) by commit 8b47299a411a, but it requires runtime writes (e.g., to i_err via errseq_set) during memory reclaim, causing a kernel panic when a write-fault occurs.
root_cause.evidence: The fix changes the swap address space declaration from `__ro_after_init` to `__read_mostly`, and the panic trace shows the failing write at `errseq_set` (called from `__filemap_set_wb_err` during `shrink_folio_list`), which would write to the read-only `swap_space` structure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Correct the annotation of `swap_space` from `__ro_after_init` to `__read_mostly` to allow writes after initialization, fixing an incorrect assumption that the variable is never written after init.
intent_record.what: Changed the annotation of the extern variable `swap_space` from `__ro_after_init` to `__read_mostly`.
intent_record.how: This allows writes to `swap_space` after system initialization, whereas before it was placed in read-only memory and any write would cause a crash or undefined behavior. The new `__read_mostly` annotation still optimizes for frequent reads but permits occasional writes, avoiding cache line bouncing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Allow runtime modification of `swap_space` by changing its section attribute from read-only after init to read-mostly.
intent_record.what: Removed comment and changed `__ro_after_init` to `__read_mostly` for `struct address_space swap_space`.
intent_record.how: The variable `swap_space` is no longer write-protected after kernel init; it can be modified at runtime, and its memory placement is adjusted for frequently read data.
